about.title: Dublin Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Dublin's mix of retail centers along Dublin Boulevard, apartment communities near Dougherty Road, and busy commercial strips on Amador Valley Boulevard means plenty of foot traffic every day — and plenty of opportunities for wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting, or unmarked hazards to go unaddressed. Under California law, a property owner or manager isn't automatically responsible just because someone got hurt on their property. You generally have to show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn people about it in time. That's why what you document in the first hours and days matters so much. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly — we're a free connection service. We match you with an independent attorney who can look at what happened at the specific Dublin property, help you understand the notice requirement, and explain your options without any pressure to sign anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Property Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law hinges on whether the owner had notice of the hazard before you were hurt. An attorney can help identify inspection logs, prior complaints, or how long a spill or defect existed.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Dublin retail and apartment properties record over surveillance video within days or weeks. Acting quickly can make the difference in whether that footage still exists when it's requested.

items.title: Navigating Comparative Fault
items.desc: Even if you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule may still allow partial recovery. An attorney can help present the facts fairly rather than let blame get shifted entirely onto you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Dublin?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim to be filed first. An attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I partly caused my own fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility for the fall. Your potential recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is decided case by case based on the evidence.

items.question: Does it matter which Dublin property I fell at?
items.answer: Yes — whether it happened at a shopping center off Dublin Boulevard, an apartment complex near Dougherty Road, or elsewhere can affect who's responsible, whether a management company is involved, and how quickly surveillance footage might be overwritten. An independent attorney can help sort out ownership and notice specific to that location.
